question.problem:
$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}3x, & 0<x<1,\,0<y<x \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}, & 0<x<1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the continuous random variables $X$ and $Y,$ for which the joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ and the marginal density function ${f}_{X}(x)$ are shown above. Find the expression of the conditional probability density function ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ for $0<x<1,\,0<y<x.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)},
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $0<x<1,\,0<y<x,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)} \\  & =\frac{3x}{3{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x}, & 0<x<1,\,0<y<x \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
